If struct Node is a self-referential structure with a pointer to itself, what is the output of the following code?

struct Node { 

    int data; 

    struct Node *next; 

}; 

 

int main() { 

    struct Node n1, n2; 

    n1.data = 10; 

    n2.data = 20; 

    n1.next = &n2; 

    printf("%d", n1.next->data); 

    return 0; 

}

sq.ANSWER:
A self referential structure is used to create data structures like linked lists, stacks, etc.

Following is an example of this kind of structure:

 struct struct_name

{

datatype

datatype name; struct_name * pointer_name;

};

A self-referential structure is one of the data structures which refer to the pointer to (points) to another structure of the same type. For example, a linked list is supposed to be a self- referential data structure. The next node of a node is being pointed, which is of the same struct type. For example,

typedef struct  listnode { void *data;

struct listnode *next;

} linked_list;

In the above example, the listnode is a self-referential structure – because the *next is of the type struct listnode.

Self-referential structures are most commonly used to implement singly linked lists, where each node stores a value and a pointer to the next node.

The structure pointer points to the address of a memory block where the Structure is being stored.

Structure pointer tells the address of a structure in memory by pointing pointer variable ptr to the structure variable.

Syntax:

1. Declaration:

struct structure_name *ptr;  

2. Initialization of the Structure Pointer:

struct structure_name *ptr = &structure_variable;  

  •  pointer ptr is pointing to the address structure_variable of the Structure

Array-Based Inventory

Product inventory[MAX_PRODUCTS];

int productCount = 0; // To keep track of the number of products in the inventory

 

  1. Insertion: Adding a New Product

 

void insertProduct(Product newProduct) {

if (productCount == MAX_PRODUCTS) { printf("Inventory is full. Cannot add new product.\n"); return;

}

 

int i;

// Find the correct position for the new product

for (i = productCount - 1; (i >= 0 && inventory[i].productID > newProduct.productID); i--) { inventory[i + 1] = inventory[i]; // Shift elements to the right

}

// Insert the new product inventory[i + 1] = newProduct;

productCount++; // Increment the product count

}

 

  1. Deletion: Removing a Product by Product ID -

void deleteProduct(int productID) { int i, pos = -1;

 

// Find the product by its ID

for (i = 0; i < productCount; i++) {

if (inventory[i].productID == productID) { pos = i;

break;

}

}

 

// If product not found if (pos == -1) {

printf("Product with ID %d not found in inventory.\n", productID); return;

}

// Shift elements to the left to fill the gap for (i = pos; i < productCount - 1; i++) {

inventory[i] = inventory[i + 1];

}

 

productCount--; // Decrement the product count

}

 

  1. Traversal: Displaying the Inventory List void displayInventory() { if (productCount == 0) {

printf("Inventory is empty.\n"); return;

}

printf("Inventory List:\n"); printf("ID\tName\t\tQuantity\tPrice\n"); printf("                                                            \n");

 

for (int i = 0; i < productCount; i++) { printf("%d\t%s\t\t%d\t\t%.2f\n", inventory[i].productID,

inventory[i].name, inventory[i].quantity, inventory[i].price);

}

}

lq.QUESTION_DESC:
You are developing an inventory management system for a small retail store. The system needs to manage a list of products, where each product has a unique product ID. The store manager requires the following to be performed.

Insertion: A new product needs to be added to the inventory. The system should place the product in the appropriate position to keep the list sorted by product ID.

Deletion: Occasionally, products may be discontinued or removed from the inventory. The system should allow the manager to delete a product by its product ID, adjusting the list accordingly.

Traversal: The manager wants to view the entire inventory list, displaying each product's details in order of product ID.

Describe how you would implement these operations using an array-based approach in C. Explain the steps involved in each operation and how the array data structure supports efficient management of the inventory.
